claims.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a direct factor Xa (F10) inhibitor whose anticancer selectivity in this screen is unlikely to reflect on-target coagulation inhibition, since most solid tumor lines do not depend on F10 for viability. The transcriptional signature (upregulation of NR3C1, GATA3, IKZF1, TGFBR2 and downregulation of CHEK1, FOS) and similarity to warfarin, etodolac, and a p38 inhibitor suggest off-target modulation of nuclear receptor and stress/MAPK signaling, so selectivity is best explained by expression of the drug's uptake/efflux transporters and of F10 itself, plus mutations that alter these pathways.

features.basis: On-target factor Xa expression is required for rivaroxaban to engage its annotated target
Glucocorticoid receptor upregulation in the virtual cell may buffer stress and reduce killing
CHEK1 downregulation in the virtual cell suggests loss of DNA-damage checkpoint protection
FOS downregulation in the virtual cell indicates impaired AP-1 stress response
TGFBR2 upregulation in the virtual cell may enhance growth-inhibitory signaling
GATA3 upregulation in the virtual cell suggests lineage-dependent transcriptional vulnerability
IKZF1 upregulation in the virtual cell may alter lymphoid transcriptional programs
P-glycoprotein efflux can lower intracellular rivaroxaban and reduce killing
BCRP efflux is a plausible route of rivaroxaban resistance
Warfarin-like transcriptional similarity suggests vitamin K pathway modulation
Similarity to a p38 inhibitor implies p38-dependent survival signaling
Similarity to etodolac suggests COX-2-dependent prostaglandin survival signaling
